Time trends within countries
The analysis of cancer trends over time can lead to useful ﬁndings in the study of diet and cancer. By looking at the change in cancer
rates in a speciﬁc population over time and comparing these rates with changes in speciﬁc factors over the same period (e.g., changes
in dietary habits), investigators can uncover possible associations supporting the dietary factors hypotheses. For example, in 1991
researchers examined vital statistics for Japanese natives and US whites that revealed changes in cancer mortality and related ante-
cedent patterns of lifestyle in the two populations (Wynder et al., 1991). These investigations uncovered that animal fat consump-
tion in Japan steadily increased from a daily level of 6.5 g per person in 1955 to 27.6 g in 1987; at the same time the Japanese rate of
colon cancer in men rose at a rapid pace; in fact, the mortality rates owing to colon cancer in men almost tripled over this time. This
evidence lent more support to the hypothesis that mortality from colon cancer in men is inﬂuenced by high dietary fat
consumption.
